reasons.C: Long, balanced periodic sentences with semicolons and double-dash asides, an urbane ironic assertiveness and a dry personal close ('I fancy it is nothing of the sort') come closest to the passage's confident, sardonic movement.
reasons.A: Has the period diction, double dashes and a parenthetical jab, but its short clipped runs and softer confiding hedges ('I know it is not a popular thing to say') are less assured than the author, and the exclamation aside edges toward imitation.
reasons.B: Plain, even, modern expository prose with no dashes, asides, irony or rhetorical turns; measured and hedged where the author is barbed and assertive.
